lead.headline: Putin repeats his territorial demands after the Abu Dhabi talks; Europe is promised a seat next round
lead.dek: ISW reads the Kremlin's post-talks statements as no movement, while Witkoff and Kushner brief Zelensky near Dublin and say Europeans will join the next meeting. Overnight Russian strikes hit Kyiv, Odesa, Rivne and Vinnytsia.

bottom_line: After two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, ISW says Putin told US envoys Russia still wants all of the four annexed oblasts and rejects foreign troops in Ukraine. The envoys then met Zelensky near Dublin and said a further meeting is scheduled with Europeans at the table. On the southern front ISW saw no Russian advances on November 11 and 12, while glide bomb use near Orikhiv is rising.

numbers.label: Russian assault attempts on the front over the past day, per Ukraine's General Staff
Russian strike drones downed or suppressed overnight November 12 to 13, per the Air Force
Glide bomb strikes a day in the Orikhiv direction, per a Ukrainian brigade spokesperson

front.summary: ISW reported no Russian advances on the Huliaipole axis or in western Zaporizhzhia Oblast on November 11 and 12, and no ground activity in the Kherson direction on November 12. Ukraine's General Staff counted nine Russian attacks in the Huliaipole sector and none in the Orikhiv and Dnipro River sectors. Glide bomb use near Orikhiv is rising, and drones are still striking civilians in Kherson city.

axes.name: Huliaipole
axes.text: Russian forces continued offensive operations on November 11 and 12 but did not advance, according to ISW. The General Staff said defenders repelled nine attacks near Ternuvate, Dolynka and Bilohiria. Ukraine's 7th Corps said it struck a launch site for Molniya-type drones in occupied Huliaipole, which is Ukraine's claim.

axes.name: Orikhiv
axes.text: ISW saw no Russian advance in western Zaporizhzhia Oblast. A Ukrainian brigade spokesperson said Russian forces are dropping 12 to 30 glide bombs a day on positions in the direction, which ISW reads as likely preparation for later offensive operations. The General Staff recorded no Russian offensive operations in the Orikhiv sector over the past day.

axes.name: Dnipro line and islands
axes.text: The General Staff recorded no Russian offensive operations in the Dnipro River sector over the past day, and ISW saw no ground activity in the Kherson direction on November 12. Ukrainian marine units say Russia used the October 27 to November 1 Oleshky ceasefire to rotate units, bring in ammunition and strengthen positions, which the Kyiv Independent reported on November 10.

axes.name: Kherson city
axes.text: ISW cites geolocated footage published on November 12 showing a drone operator of Russia's 98th Airborne Division striking a civilian woman driving a car in Kherson city. ISW describes this as part of a long-running pattern of drone attacks on civilians there.

map_events.summary: ISW cites geolocated footage of a Russian 98th Airborne Division drone operator striking a woman driving in Kherson city.

map_events.summary: The General Staff recorded 13 attacks in the Kostiantynivka sector, the busiest of the day with Pokrovsk.

map_events.title: Kyiv hospital damaged
map_events.summary: Debris from a Russian drone hit a medical facility in Kyiv, partly destroying a second floor and injuring three patients, the Health Ministry said.

map_events.summary: Mayor Klitschko said one person was killed and eight injured in overnight and daytime strikes on November 12.

map_events.summary: Two people were killed and five hospitalized in a Russian attack on Odesa on the morning of November 13, regional officials said.

map_events.title: Apartment block hit in Rivne
map_events.summary: Six people, including two children, were injured when a Russian drone struck a residential building; 42 residents were evacuated.

map_events.summary: Zelensky met Witkoff and Kushner at an airbase outside Dublin after their Moscow meeting with Putin.

map_events.summary: Moldovan police found drone fragments in a vineyard near Antonesti, about 10 kilometers from Odesa Oblast. The origin is under examination.

map_events.summary: Poland's defense minister said the Pentagon has greenlit a permanent US troop presence; the White House decides in early December.

sections.summary: The day was dominated by what the Abu Dhabi talks produced: ISW sees no Russian shift, while the US envoys say Europe will join the next round. Russian strikes continued on cities as air defense supplies and satellite service restrictions drew warnings from Kyiv.

items.headline: ISW says Putin held to his demands after the Abu Dhabi talks
items.summary: ISW's assessment says Putin told Witkoff and Kushner that Russia's own border is the only clear demarcation line and rejected foreign troops in Ukraine. ISW concludes the Kremlin has not moved from its original demands. This is ISW's reading of Russian statements.

items.headline: Witkoff says another round of talks is scheduled
items.summary: After meeting Zelensky near Dublin, Witkoff said the next meeting of negotiating teams is already on the schedule and that Trump wants to lead efforts to end the war. He called the Abu Dhabi meeting constructive.

items.headline: Zelensky tells Rutte interceptor shortages and Starshield limits hurt air defense
items.summary: Zelensky said Russia fired 115 missiles in the first week of November and that restrictions on Starshield service limit Ukraine's ability to stop jet-powered Shahed drones. He thanked NATO for its willingness to help with PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles.

items.headline: Russian drones hit 24 locations overnight as air defense downs 80 of 117
items.summary: Ukraine's Air Force said 117 strike drones, 63 of them jet-powered, were launched from the evening of November 12. Strikes hit Kyiv, Odesa and Rivne, among other places.

items.headline: Ukraine confirms Omsk refinery strike 2,500 kilometers from its border
items.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces said they struck the Omsk refinery on November 11, the farthest Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian refinery so far. The unit's own statement is the main source for the damage.

sections.summary: Army Times coverage centered on Pentagon policy and Congress, with a new Army school activated and a veterans bill passed in a disputed voice vote. A soldier's arrest in Britain on suspicion of aiding Russian intelligence also drew official comment.

items.headline: Army activates its Public Affairs School at Fort Meade
items.summary: The Army formally activated the U.S. Army Public Affairs School last month and announced it this week. Col. Kamil Sztalkoper takes over as commandant from Col. Stacy M. Hopwood.

items.headline: From November 9: Hegseth orders 33 changes to military service colleges
items.summary: A memorandum released on November 9 directs the colleges to use AI war games in place of long written dissertations and to end lifetime tenure for newly hired civilian faculty. It also asks them to ensure most full-time faculty have military experience.

items.headline: House passes veterans benefits package by disputed voice vote
items.summary: The Take Care of America's Veterans Act passed on Veterans Day with more than 60 provisions. Its most contested measure would change how sleep apnea and tinnitus are rated, potentially lowering some future compensation, and veterans groups are divided.

items.headline: From November 10: US soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of assisting Russia
items.summary: British police said a 41-year-old senior US soldier was arrested near Gloucester under the National Security Act. FBI Director Kash Patel called the allegations of the utmost concern.

sections.summary: Fort Knox news in the window was thin; the newest official item found is from November 9.

items.headline: From November 9: Fort Knox recruiter coaches high school football as a volunteer
items.summary: A Fort Knox statement profiles Sgt. 1st Class Larry Barner, an Army Recruiting Command recruiter who mentors students and coaches wide receivers and cornerbacks for the Fort Knox High School team. The piece illustrates the Army value of selfless service.

sections.summary: European leaders spent the day in Dublin deciding who speaks for the bloc in Ukraine talks, with a decision possibly pushed to a special summit. Sanctions, accession and a possible permanent US presence in Poland were also on the agenda.

items.headline: EU leaders weigh who should represent Europe in peace talks
items.summary: Euronews reports that Costa and Kallas are both floated, and that the decision may slip to the special summit at the end of the month. Meloni wants a clear mandate, while Tusk said Poland does not feel excluded.

items.headline: Zelensky says Europe will be in the negotiating team next time
items.summary: Zelensky said Europe will take part directly in the next round, and Kushner said no deal can be concluded without Europeans at the table. Euronews notes the Kremlin played down the prospect.

items.headline: UK targets all of Russia's top 10 oil producers with new sanctions
items.summary: The UK Foreign Ministry said the November 12 package makes Britain the only country to have sanctioned all ten. Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to press other nations at the Dublin summit for more economic pressure.

items.headline: Ireland aims to open Ukraine's last two EU negotiating clusters by year end
items.summary: Prime Minister Micheal Martin said three clusters are open and he wants the remaining two opened before Ireland's Council presidency ends on December 31. He cited the 21st sanctions package and ongoing disbursement of the EU support loan.

items.headline: Poland says Pentagon has greenlit a permanent US troop presence
items.summary: Poland's defense minister said the final decision rests with the White House in early December. Sites west of the Vistula, including Bydgoszcz, Poznan, Szczecin and Wroclaw, have been visited.

upcoming.title: Special European Council
upcoming.detail: Von der Leyen said the Commission will present an option paper on Ukraine's 2027 financing and the 22nd sanctions package at the summit on 26 and 27 November; the EU envoy question may also be decided.

upcoming.title: White House decision on a permanent US base in Poland, expected in early December
upcoming.detail: Poland's defense minister said the decision is due in early December; the exact day has not been given.

upcoming.title: Ireland's EU Council presidency ends
upcoming.detail: Ireland aims to open Ukraine's remaining two accession clusters before this date.

audio.script:
Good morning. This is the Morning Dispatch for Friday, November 13, 2026.

Here is the bottom line. After two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, the Institute for the Study of War says Vladimir Putin has not moved from his original demands. The American envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, then met President Zelensky near Dublin and said another meeting is already scheduled, with Europeans at the table. On the southern front, the institute saw no Russian advances on November 11 and 12. But Russian glide bomb use near Orikhiv is rising. And overnight, Russian drones again struck cities across Ukraine.

We start with the southern front. Everything here comes from the Institute for the Study of War assessment of November 12, and from the daily update of Ukraine's General Staff, reported by Ukrinform.

On the Huliaipole axis, the institute says Russian forces kept up offensive operations on November 11 and 12, but did not advance. The General Staff says Ukrainian defenders repelled nine attacks near Ternuvate, Dolynka and Bilohiria. Separately, Ukraine's 7th Corps says it struck a launch site for Molniya type strike drones in occupied Huliaipole. That is a Ukrainian claim, and the institute relays it without independent confirmation.

In western Zaporizhzhia, near Orikhiv, the institute again saw no Russian advance. The General Staff recorded no Russian offensive operations in the Orikhiv sector over the past day. But a spokesperson for a Ukrainian brigade there says Russia is dropping between twelve and thirty guided glide bombs every day on Ukrainian positions. The institute reads that as likely preparation for later offensive operations. That is the institute's assessment, not a confirmed plan.

On the Dnipro River line in Kherson Oblast, the General Staff recorded no Russian offensive operations, and the institute saw no ground activity on November 12. The Kyiv Independent reported on November 10 that Ukrainian marine units say Russia used the ceasefire around Oleshky, from October 27 to November 1, to rotate units, bring in ammunition and strengthen positions. That is the Ukrainian military's account. Ukraine's human rights ombudsman said neither side had reported violations.

In Kherson city, the institute cites geolocated footage published on November 12. It shows a drone operator from Russia's 98th Airborne Division striking a civilian woman who was driving a car. The institute says drone operators have long hunted civilians in the city. Because the footage is geolocated, the institute treats the event as confirmed.

Now the wider war. The General Staff says Russian forces made 175 assault attempts over the past day. The busiest areas were the Kostiantynivka sector, with 13 attacks, and the Pokrovsk sector, with 11. Ukraine's Air Assault Forces commander, Oleh Apostol, told journalists that the Russian pace of advance has slowed considerably, and that capturing a tree line in a month is hardly an operational success. That is one Ukrainian commander's view.

On the diplomacy, the institute says that after the Abu Dhabi talks Putin told Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow that Russia's own border, which in Russian law includes the four annexed regions, is the only clear demarcation line. He also said that foreign troops in Ukraine are absolutely unacceptable. The institute concludes that the Kremlin has not changed its demands. After Moscow, the envoys met Zelensky at a military airbase outside Dublin. Witkoff said the next meeting of negotiating teams is already on the schedule and called the Abu Dhabi round constructive. Euronews reports that Zelensky said Europe will be in the negotiating team next time, and that Kushner said no deal can be concluded without Europeans at the table. Euronews adds that the Kremlin played down that prospect.

Overnight from November 12 to 13, Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 117 strike drones, 63 of them jet powered. Air defenses shot down or suppressed 80. Hits were recorded at 24 locations. Ukrinform reports a Kyiv medical facility was damaged, with three patients injured. In Rivne, six people, including two children, were injured when a drone hit an apartment building. In Odesa, regional officials say two people were killed and five hospitalized. On November 12, the mayor of Kyiv said one person was killed and eight injured in strikes on the capital.

President Zelensky told NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that Russia fired 115 missiles in the first week of November alone. He said Ukraine faces a shortage of anti ballistic interceptors, and that renewed restrictions on Starshield satellite service limit its ability to stop jet powered Shahed drones. He thanked NATO for its willingness to help with Patriot missiles.

Ukraine also reached far into Russia. Its Special Operations Forces say they struck the Omsk oil refinery on November 11, about twenty five hundred kilometers from the border. They say it is the farthest Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian refinery so far. The damage is not yet independently assessed.

Now the Army. Army Times reports the Army has formally activated its Public Affairs School at Fort Meade, Maryland. Colonel Kamil Sztalkoper takes over as commandant. Army Times also reports that on November 9 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth released a memorandum with 33 directives for military service colleges. They would use A I war games in place of long written dissertations, end lifetime tenure for newly hired civilian faculty, and require most full time faculty to have military experience.

In Congress, the House passed the Take Care of America's Veterans Act by voice vote on Veterans Day. It has more than 60 provisions, including support for surviving spouses and caregivers. Its most contested measure would change how the V A rates sleep apnea and tinnitus, which could lower some future compensation. Veterans groups are divided, and Army Times reports the vote happened while Democratic leaders were off the floor.

Army Times also reported on November 10 that a 41 year old senior American soldier was arrested near Gloucester, in England, on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence. FBI Director Kash Patel called the allegations of the utmost concern.

On Fort Knox, news in the window was thin. The newest official item we found is from November 9. A Fort Knox statement profiles Sergeant First Class Larry Barner, an Army Recruiting Command recruiter who volunteers as an assistant coach for the Fort Knox High School football team, as an example of the Army value of selfless service.

Now Europe. European leaders met in Dublin, and Euronews reports the central question is who speaks for Europe in the Ukraine talks. Council President Antonio Costa and foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas have both been floated. Italy's prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, wants someone with a clear mandate. Poland's prime minister, Donald Tusk, said Poland does not feel excluded. If no decision is taken, it may move to a special summit at the end of the month.

The United Kingdom announced new sanctions on November 12. Its foreign ministry says Britain is now the only country to have sanctioned all ten of Russia's top oil producers. Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin says he wants Ukraine's remaining two accession clusters opened before Ireland's presidency of the Council of the EU ends on December 31. Three clusters are now open.

In Poland, the defense minister says the Pentagon has greenlit a permanent American troop presence, with the final decision at the White House in early December. That is the Polish minister's account. The Pentagon's own statement did not mention a base, according to Army Times. And in Moldova, police found drone fragments in a vineyard near the village of Antonesti, about ten kilometers from Odesa Oblast. Their origin is still being examined.

Finally, the days ahead. On November 26 and 27, EU leaders hold a special European Council. Ursula von der Leyen says the Commission will present an options paper on financing Ukraine in 2027, and the twenty second sanctions package, there. In early December, the White House is due to decide on a permanent American base in Poland. And on December 31, Ireland's presidency of the EU Council ends.

That is the Morning Dispatch. Every claim here is linked to its source on the page.
